title: They dont look polished enough to keep me interested
author: Square_Reason_6490
selftext:
https://youtu.be/dmw7iTQvTRo?is=ZPzUQOMHGZlLMjqR

I saw this on YouTube and it made me laugh a little. These Al generated projects are technically impressive, but they're usually super buggy and don't feel like games Id actually want to play.  
I wonder if the Al game dev community would benefit more from building tiny, polished experiences instead of huge ambitious demos. A 5minute game that's genuinely fun probably teaches us more than a massive project that barely works.  
Im guilty of the opposite too Im building something much bigger and keep hesitating to share it.

Curious what everyone else thinks:  
Should Al devs focus on polished micro-games first, or keep pushing ambitious one shot or “I made this while I drank a coffee!!”?

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Doesn't matter. "Small and polished" doesnt automatically mean fun. 

Just think of the last "small and polished microgame" you actually played. 

You are just regurgitating empty idea that sounds right on the surface (but you probably dont even follow)

I think the benefit of ai game dev is the speed and flexibility. May be well let people experiment and go wild

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body:
What idea am I regurgitating? And what am I not following? The benefit is speed yes, but made a game in 5 mins is only speed, pretty much any code you generate with AI already has the speed applied any art you make has speed applied but speed doesn’t have to mean careless. 

I’m also not saying people can’t experiment and more so I think I have any control on what people do or release I’m posing a idea a pov a approach I actually care very much about the craft of game creation ai use or not I think it’s all of value but the lead for ai game dev should not be only speed with no care

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
The whole idea of polish = interest 

It doesnt work that way. It is just something devs on reddit love to say to each other (and then nobody touched these polished demos or microgames, whatever you call them)

Just do what you preach and you would realize that craft/care doesnt mean as much as you think it does. Its just idea + execution in the end

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: I didn’t realize I’m preaching I said my pov and asked a question, and I am doin what I think is best, going fast but with what I believe is care and will share wip when I think it will benefit others and maybe inspire someone else to make something great or give someone a great experience

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
And I gave you the answer:care/polish doesnt mean as much as you think it does. 

But its fine. I suppose it is something each dev has to experience personally to understand 

Remind me when your wip is out

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Help me understand why care and polish doesn’t mean so much?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
Players are not devs. They don't "score" your game based on quality/care. They just want something fun to play

You can perfectly execute a boring game and the end result would be the same as a unpolished boring game 

In fact, many devs go down that road because they are obsessed with quality (they are afraid to experiment or do anything new)

If you have a creative idea and your execution is subpar, it is at least a fixable problem

The opposite of that is most of the game posts you see on reddit. (But it is like a rabbit hole because polish is never enough so these devs just double/triple down on quality/care)

replies.author: denzelgamedev
replies.body: You having an idea and executing it doesn't really matter if in the end your game does not have quality. I'm not saying that I achieved that quality because just like the others I'm iterating on it to eventually get to a satisfying result but this idea of just doing more and more projects without caring if it's playable or if it's even fun is why everyone associates AI games with slop.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
It is the opposite actually if you look at the past successful indie games. Some friend slops and simulator games dont even play that well

Some games are also carried by the devs' popularity.

Ai games are slops not because of the quality; its mostly because 1) they are boring clones and 2) creators are too afraid to take risks (ironically, they want quality so they scale down to only something they can accomplish confidently)

So this very idea of quality/idea is actually leading devs into making slops

If devs actually go with more ambitions and courage (the willingness to make something hard), they may have a better shot

E.g. the typical ai browser games are polished and boring...

replies.author: denzelgamedev
replies.body:
Most AI game developers have little to no experience at making games. Asking them to make a game with more ambition and courage seems like a bad advice when most of them have no idea how certain aspects of the game may impact the player, whether it's the visuals or gameplay. If they even think of that instead of just accepting whatever the AI suggests them to do.

This friend slops and simulator games do play well, they achieve what they intended to do. You might say that most of them are not really fun for you (which I would agree, specially friend slops) but in the end it was a simple gameplay that they polished until it was considered fun. If they do not succeed they didn't lose much time and at least learned something and perhaps made a little money from it.

Not saying that you shouldn't try to make big games first time, it might end up well and you will learn a lot either way but you're more likely to lose yourself on the way, work on something that was a bad idea on the start and give up because of it.

I think you have valid thoughts but I just can't agree with the idea overall for the reasons mentioned before. Have a good one mate!

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
Failing to make games is also experience gained. If they are ai game devs, it wouldn't take them months to fail anyways. 

The important difference is that those successful devs already have some players when they polish the gameplay. The idea carried the project, it wasnt quality/care

I think the community obsession with quality/care is how we end up with boring games; we are encouraging devs to make simple games that nobody would play. Some devs are too afraid to share anything even because they dont think they have enough quality/care.

replies.author: denzelgamedev
replies.body:
You're right about the experience part, I did mentioned that too. About the quality/care... What stops the ai game dev from making a big game as you have mentioned while still showing care and many iterations with it? I think that would be a good scenario as well, you don't have to just show care and make games with quality that are small.

And I disagree with the "it wasn't the quality/care", of course it was. The players followed to thei next project because the previous had that much quality and care (for example, Deltarune).

My problem is those one shot games that ruin the image of AI game devs because there's little to no effort put into it and the result is really bad. Not saying that all one shot games are bad because I haven't seen them all but the ones that I've seen (which were plenty) can barely be called games.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
A good example is the ai text based browser game genre. Those devs make a calculated decision because its hard to make polished animation with ai. They avoid taking risks to accomplish a quality product. 

One-shot games are usually just tech demos. I dont know what kind of image you think we have (it doesnt matter what we do, using ai = no effort to many people regardless)

People who make one-shot games are mostly just testing AIs anyways. I personally appreciate the fact that they are spending tokens/limits so I dont have to

replies.author: denzelgamedev
replies.body:
I also appreciate that, it shows evolution but the results are still bad... Until in the future they aren't :)

About the people thinking "AI = Slop", it's not a reason to prove them right by making bad quality games with ai. If anything we should do the opposite and convince the people who haven't formulated an opinion about it or even change the minds of the people who had that thought.

Of course you don't have to actually care about this stuff, just do what you like with AI. You're the one paying for it, you should use it as you enjoy! I'm still going to have my opinion on it and so will you.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
Those people are just brigading. Some devs go the opposite way i.e. handcrafted, no AI, took them 2-3 years, blah blah, and they dont get anywhere as well (because in the end, effort/care doesnt generate interest)

I think if you are already embracing the AI way, you may as well embrace the new mindset too. Obsessing with quality/care/craftsmanship is just holding people back. 

I think creativity/originality should come before anything else.

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Oh man for a guy who wants to break all the rules you sure set a lot of rules, “care” does not always mean time it means make good decisions and choices we can give people the same amount of time to complete a task and often we will see skill gaps I think to benefit the community it’s best to move things forward not just make stuff the challenge with these new tools is a bit of restraint without what separates your output from anyone else’s or how about when agents get even better? What do you even need a person for? Just hit “make game button” added to our phones and keyboard

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
the irony is that the belief in quality/care/effort doesn't lead to good decisions. It sounds counterintuitive but being too concerned with quality basically lead to boring decisions. (there is also the issue of dev pride so some devs go out of their way to present quality)

in a similar sense, those one-shot vibe coders are also falling victims to the same thinking: they feel the need to make a clone of some existing games for the familiarly etc. 

I can't see the future but some pro AI people definitely think AI can solve gamedev and it literally would be like hitting "make game button" 

anyway, your ideas and beliefs are pretty mainstream so don't worry about it. I am just offering you my perspective on things after seeing it play out a few times (personally and watching/follow other devs' projects)

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: I don’t agree with your social philosophy on what’s happening with AI at all but I have to say your game projects speak very differently it looks like you are putting a certain level of care into them and the variety of genres and styles speaks volumes. I think you are reading comments wrong at times on who is brigading or not

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
yes, I am basically coming from a "been there, done that" angle. effort/care alone doesn't generate enough interest. you can get a pat on the back by fellow devs but that gets old after a while.

it goes without saying that a certain level of care/effort is expected to give the game a chance but it is really not as big of an edge as people think it is

some devs are ex-AAA or ex-indie studio and they think they can just make a successful project because they have the quality/craftmanship (which they do) but it doesn't really work that way

I think it is just a matter of perspective in the end. I am definitely at a point where I am seeing past those reddit dev culture about the effort/care etc. It is a bunch of people romancing certain ideals because they cant see past the wall in front of them; the goal isn't actually behind the wall.

replies.author: LorenzoMorini
replies.body: Small and polished microgame is the motto of lot of game jam games. Many are very very fun.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
Game jam winners usually have some addicting gameplay figured out. It doesnt have much to do with quality/care. (Winning a jam doesn't automatically lead to anything fruitful either)

The internet is full of polished merge/infinite runner/object drop games/etc

But sure, keep pushing for devs to make another boring game with quality/care

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Maybe I shouldn’t have used the word “polish” I think the fun is often found in the polish I don’t mean polish as graphics sound or presentation meaning “does it feel fun to shoot, move, kill things, jump etc”…game mechanic feel fun and addictive equals polish to me. I believe I see a lot of first pass Greenbox type demos maybe less than that and are base proofs of concepts most of the time not even at the level you would use to convince a team to get excited to work on the project right now it’s more get excited you can make stuff, I’m looking for get excited you can actually make something good one major thing I learned today is I need to be way more careful on how I post because I’m not trying to create bad vibes

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
You are comparing apples and oranges. ai game dev has an emphasis on the tech aspect so you will see a lot of tech demos. Those are not proof of concepts for gameplay or anything.

You are not excited because you are not looking for the right stuff in those posts. When I see a one-shot post, I look for tech progress etc. There is a reason people are required to mention the ai workflow in posts

I am not sure what you expect but the average game wip post on this sub or any other indie sub isn't going to contain amazing, exciting gameplay. (If you want, just go by posts with triple digit upvotes, those are rare)

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body:
Well I just found one 

https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/

I think I’ve been looking for the right stuff, and still working on refining my definition of polish and probably never using it again when posting unless I’m being ultra specific the way you locked onto that one word is crazy to me, I don’t think I was ever clear about what I thought was inspiring and I disagree with ai game devs are separate than other game devs or maybe you are right there are some people that are just making stuff with ai and there artists or game devs musicians etc that are using ai as a tool to help produce their vision and maybe at this moment in time it’s too hard to see the separation well for me at least I’ve learned a lot from hearing your counter points even tho I hate them 🤣

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
You can call it craftmanship/care/effort/quality but my point is the same: it is too much of a dev's perspective

Before AI, I have seen enough posts where devs beg for others to check out their carefully crafted demos. It is a dead end imo

The lack of quality definitely can drag down a otherwise good game but most of the time it is not the case. 

I think a lot of it is the dev culture + perfectionism + insecurity 

Devs whom I have this familiar argument with usually dont come back anything released so I am becoming more and more certain that it is the wrong mentality

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body:
Scope isn't necessarily the problem when it comes to polish, although it can contribute. The problem is that polish is the remaining 80% of the work and it's boring and thankless. 

It's not an AI specific thing either, this happens all the time in traditional game dev communities. Someone makes something, gets excited, releases it, obviously buggy and unpolished.

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: True, but it seems like so much of these demos is unpolished like it doesn’t need to be Valve quality but why not polish one part beyond the one shot? I also think part of the mastery will be in being able to address the errors the ai made having control of what is created so maybe that’s what’s I’m saying it does seem most of these demos I’m seeing are showing true control it’s very much like the beginning of image generation 3-4 years ago

replies.author: TechgeekOne
replies.body:
It makes more sense when you remember that a lot of the people posting these demos probably haven't built and shipped a game before. They legitimately don't know how and it's a learning process for them.

The other half I'd blame on the tools. Yeah AI can get you up and running quickly with basically nothing but a rendering library and a dream, but there's a reason most serious games ship on a battle tested engine. The more you build from scratch the more you have to test and fix before it's polished. Most of the demos I've seen are built from scratch on a web render library and thus lack that polish. It's not like you can just plug your AI of choice into Unity/Unreal/Godot/your engine of choice yet either. There's still real work involved to make that workflow happen easily and it's woefully under supported or painful to use.

"oh i have a cool idea, let's try it" -> "huh so many bugs. AI fix them!" -> "huh actually it isn't that fun

comments.author: ReleasePossible2731
comments.body:
My guess is that it’s not about AI or not. Most games out there aren’t really hitting the fun mark, thats why not every game gets bought or downloaded any meaningful number of times. My guess with AI games specifically is that people who make them are not game devs. They are vibe coders, AI evangelists and curious people. So they aren’t necessarily after a playable game, they are seeking the most striking thing they can do with AI and game is one of the examples.   
Not to say that non-game-devs aren’t capable of building fun games. More to stay they are likely after a different sort of use case

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Very good point. The selfish side in me wants to think you are 100% correct and that the project I’m working on will be as awesome as I think it is and will be one of the great made with AI northstars 🤣

replies.author: ReleasePossible2731
replies.body: might as well be

comments.author: LocoMod
comments.body: A lot of people are finding out that the last 20% of a project takes 80% of the time. Things are easy. Until they are not. And projects that grow quickly grow faster than the ability of the human to process it. AI is making this worse. But eventually we will figure it out. We are still in the early days.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: Share early, get feedback good or bad, take that feedback and improve. Better than making a complete game that no one wants.

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
Neither. People should spend time and effort on their games refining and improving them. Whether they use AI or not. 

AI can't tell you if your mix of gameplay features are fun. At some point you need to step in and make some decisions. Even if you get the AI to help you with that.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
Just because you give everyone a canvas and a paintbrush it doesn't mean everyone can now create a good painting.

This time period is very much like the old days of Flash games. Flash made it a lot easier for people to make online games so there was a flood of them. You could go to web pages with hundreds of them. Occasionally you would get a gem but the majority of them were either crap or games that were extremely shallow and fun for 2 minutes until you moved onto the next one. This is likely what the amateur AI game space is going to look like.

Making a fun game takes creativeness, time and skill even with AI use. AI doesn't replace any of that so the majority of people building games using AI as a crutch for their lack of knowledge or skill will produce slop or "tech demos" that go nowhere.

comments.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
comments.body: There seems to be a lot of context missing here. I watch this guy, he just makes content 1 shooting models based off his community's requests.

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Sounds interesting I have come to realize the “look how fast I made this” is not a good of the medium at all, it seems to only fuel resentment and hate and gives ai users the “lazy” label 😔

comments.author: tschilpi
comments.body: Fundamentally the things that are crucial for a good game like proper game design, crispy visuals, progression, a tight loop, a unique premise, etc. are things that AI can assist with but AI can't generate/replicate it. You still have to know what you're doing and making a good game is as hard as ever, especially now with the sea of copycats and low-effort projects, where you might have a genuinely good game but it could get lumped under these if you mention the use of AI.

comments.author: No-Run-7324
comments.body: Making games with ai is the same making anything else, start small then move up. Its the same advice I give for traditional gamedevs or anybody else learning something. There are fundamentals that you have to develop and you are lucky enough now to be able to practice finding the fun in games at a relatively rapid pace. You can always make the fun game larger or incorporate aspects of that smaller game into a larger game later. Whats most important for you ai gamedevs right now would be try8ng to mastering feel. All the bugs and jankyness can/will be worked out as llms get better but the feel of your game is what will separate your game from other people ai developed game. So build a lot of small games and learn to tweak them and you'll be better off in the long run.
